title: The Euclidean coefficient norm can be computed in any orthonormal basis (parent Step 3)
statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ, every orthonormal basis u = (u_0,…,u_{P−1}) of ℝ^P (OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Eucl P)) and every k-covector φ on ℝ^P (Covector (Eucl P) k): covectorEuclideanNorm(φ)² = Σ_{I : {0,…,k−1} → [P] strictly increasing} φ(u_{I(0)},…,u_{I(k−1)})². In Lean the sum runs over all I : Fin k → Fin P, with summand 0 for I that are not strictly increasing. So SimonGMT's coefficient norm, defined with the standard basis, takes the same value in every orthonormal basis.
lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (u : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Eucl P)) (φ : Covector (Eucl P) k), covectorEuclideanNorm φ ^ 2 = ∑ I : Fin k → Fin P, if StrictMono I then (φ (fun i => u (I i))) ^ 2 else 0
